Molecular choice and present claim boundary

CB7/PEG remains the strongest chemical lead from this investigation. Aqueous CB7 pumping and exterior crosslinking of allyl-functionalized CB7 have been reported separately. The accessible evidence does not establish their required intersection: ordered functionalized/native rings that retain sliding after selective connection. 
pure.kaist.ac.kr
+1

The original crystallography sharpens the mapping problem: CB7 has a 5.4 Å portal, 7.3 Å equatorial cavity, and 9.1 Å height. It is a barrel with narrow portals, not a uniform 5.4 Å bore. PEG’s experimentally matched persistence length of approximately 3.7–3.8 Å supplies statistical stiffness, not a hard minimum bend radius. These facts neither validate nor disprove the proposed retention mechanism; they specify what the joint molecular calculation must resolve.

Established convex-route mechanics already supplies convexity under suitable constitutive assumptions; the remaining advance must establish those assumptions from the molecular contact and retained inventory.
